title: ergonomic-session-proxy-and-adaptive-retry-presets-py-ts-go
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: ergonomics around session lifecycle and retry policies across our three SDKs remains a frequent source of customer confusion. This PR introduces a small, language-idiomatic SessionProxy abstraction plus a set of adaptive retry presets that provide sane defaults for streaming and request/response flows. The goal is parity of behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go without forcing a single API shape. Summary of changes: 1) Add SessionProxy (py/ts/go) - a thin ergonomic wrapper over the existing session/credential primitives that exposes: start(), lease(), refresh(), and close() helpers; built-in exponential-with-jitter retry hooks; and a lightweight health-check callback. 2) Adaptive retry presets - preconfigured profiles (interactive, background, batch) that tune backoff windows and idempotency rules. SDKs wire these into their stream managers so clients get better reconnect behavior out of the box. 3) Cross-SDK config normalization - introduce session_config schema with explicit fields (lease_ttl, refresh_margin, retry_profile) and mapping utilities in each SDK to keep platform behavior consistent. 4) Minimal public API renames: SessionManager -> SessionProxy alias (backwards compatible shim) and RetryConfig -> RetryProfile (alias + deprecation warnings). 5) Tests and examples: add end-to-end fixtures that run the same scripted session scenario against local mock server to assert parity of lease refresh timing and retry window alignment. 6) Docs and migration guide: update quickstart snippets and add migration note describing aliasing and recommended upgrade path. Why this is safe: migration shims maintain old names, and defaults are conservative. Breaking changes: none (no removal of existing symbols); we do however add deprecation warnings for the old RetryConfig name to encourage migration. Performance/behavior notes: adaptive retry presets reduce median reconnection time for streaming tears by ~18% in our perf lab for typical interactive profiles (see bench notes below). Checklist: - [x] Implement SessionProxy in Python - [x] Implement SessionProxy in TypeScript and Go with idiomatic signatures - [x] Add adaptive retry presets and mapping utilities - [x] Add unit + integration tests that exercise cross-sdk parity - [x] Update docs / quickstarts / migration guide - [x] Bump patch/minor versions in each SDK package files for release - [x] CI green and e2e smoke verified Bench notes: See perf/benchmarks/session-reconnect/README.md for lab numbers comparing legacy vs adaptive profiles. Migration notes: existing code using SessionManager or RetryConfig continue to work; consumers are encouraged to switch to SessionProxy.start() and to select a RetryProfile (interactive/batch/background) instead of hand-rolling backoff. Implementation details: the SessionProxy implements a small state machine with explicit states (idle, leased, refreshing, closed). Lease renewals are scheduled respecting refresh_margin and are cancellable on close(). RetryProfile maps to a {base_delay, max_delay, max_attempts, jitter_pct, idempotent_safe} tuple internally; streaming reconnection logic consults idempotent_safe to decide whether to resume or fallback to cold-start. Cross-language parity was validated by running the session scenario against a deterministic mock that simulates auth TTL jitter and transient network resets. Related: ENG-7421, PM-328, SUP-9142.
commits: a1b2c3d: add python SessionProxy class and unit tests
d4e5f6a: add ts SessionProxy, map config schema and docs
b7c8d9e: add go SessionProxy and compatibility shims
f0e1d2c: add adaptive retry presets and mapping utilities
c3b4a5f: update examples, quickstarts, and migration doc
e6f7a8b: fix ts lint issues reported in CI
review_comments: Liam Chen: Could we avoid naming the abstraction 'Proxy' if it implies network proxying? Suggest SessionFacade or SessionHandle. Also request explicit lifecycle docstring for start/close semantics.
Maya Patel (author): Chose 'Proxy' to convey thin mediation of existing session primitives; added docstring and example to clarify semantics. Open to renaming in a follow-up if patterns diverge.
Sofia Ramirez: Tests look good. In TS lint run we hit rule 'no-explicit-any' on the mapping util — please tighten the types.
Maya Patel: tightened types and added narrow generics to mapping util; updated tests accordingly.
Ethan Park: Do the adaptive profiles add any telemetry? We should emit a feature flag metric when a non-default profile is used.
Maya Patel: added lightweight counter telemetry (session.profile.selected) and unit tests that assert the counter increments.
release_notes: Added SessionProxy abstraction with adaptive RetryProfiles (interactive/background/batch). Backwards-compatible aliases for SessionManager and RetryConfig remain supported; RetryConfig is deprecated and will be removed after two releases. New telemetry: session.profile.selected counter. See migration guide in docs/quickstarts/session.md.
suggested_migration: Replace SessionManager with SessionProxy (thin alias exists). Prefer using RetryProfile.{interactive,background,batch} instead of custom backoff configs. Example: sp = SessionProxy(config=SessionConfig(retry_profile=RetryProfile.interactive)); sp.start()
notes: This PR was intentionally conservative: shims keep existing semantics while enabling a future incremental rollout of stronger ergonomics across languages. Follow-up work proposed: unify telemetry schema for session lifecycle and add server-side hooks to report observed renewal latency.
changelog_entry: SDK: session ergonomics - add SessionProxy and adaptive retry presets (py/ts/go); deprecate RetryConfig alias -> RetryProfile; bump SDK versions.
